# Board of County Commissioners, Wabaunsee County v. Umbehr — frozen neutral packet

**Stage:** Fresh neutral validation, commitment-free.
**Event:** No.94-1654; argued November28, 1995; merits decision group June28, 1996.
**Channel and scope:** §1254(1) review of the Tenth Circuit, 44 F.3d876, January4, 1995, rehearing denied February10. The question is protection against retaliatory termination of an existing contractor relationship for public criticism, with government interests, causation and defenses kept separate.

## Corrected record and procedural frame

The existing 1985 renewable arrangement followed a 1981 contract. The county **did not itself buy trash-hauling services**. Cities could endorse and ratify the agreement, and were not required to participate. They could leave on ninety days' notice. The agreement renewed yearly unless a party gave sixty days' termination notice or ninety days' notice to renegotiate. County and participating cities promised not to engage another residential-refuse provider while it operated. Do not convert the agreement into an at-will direct procurement contract.

Umbehr served six of seven cities, criticized landfill rates, public-record charges, asserted open-meetings violations and road/bridge management at meetings and in newspapers. His accusations are speech; their underlying truth was not adjudicated. An attempted 1990 termination failed and the contract renewed. January1991 termination followed another two-to-one vote. Heiser and Spencer supported termination. McClure opposed the earlier action and was out of office by effective termination. Umbehr later contracted directly with five of six served cities; those arrangements do not conclusively negate injury from loss of exclusivity, coordinated negotiation or notice protections.

For summary judgment the district court **assumed**, without trial findings, employee-equivalent speech protection, motivating retaliation and injury. It entered judgment on categorical contractor status and alternatively personal immunity; McClure separately prevailed on causation. The Tenth Circuit rejected categorical constitutional exclusion and remanded the surviving official-capacity claims, while affirming personal immunity and McClure's disposition. The current review does not reopen those latter judgments. Standing is supported below by asserted monetary loss and valuable contractual benefits; no property entitlement is needed merely to state the speech theory.

The source-specific lower opinion corrects the section-I generic “no conflict” line. There is an acknowledged circuit conflict, including the Seventh Circuit's contractor approach. That makes review intelligible but does not decide the proper extension.

## Strong competing legal positions and supported alternatives

**Commissioners' position:** Contract form, the contractor's operational independence and other clients, government responsibility for services, and retained termination power can justify a different relationship than public employment. Extending employee litigation can burden effective administration. A narrower alternative would retain the government's actual service-interest showing and Mt. Healthy defense. None of those policy submissions establishes the actual motive for this termination.

**Umbehr's position:** He remains a citizen subject to economic retaliation for criticism; lack of tenure or employment cannot alone make a retaliatory condition lawful. Contractors may lack many workplace disruption concerns. He seeks stronger protection for viewpoint retaliation or, at least, employee-derived protection. His proposed remand limited to motive/independent reason is advocacy, not an already adjudicated finding that the speech satisfies every applicable test.

Independent paths include:
1. Affirm the Tenth Circuit's rejection of categorical exclusion and adopt an appropriately explained Pickering analogy, preserving public concern, genuine governmental interests, causation and a preponderance same-decision defense for proceedings below. Do not declare liability on assumed summary-judgment facts.
2. Protect this existing relationship on a narrower unconstitutional-conditions basis while reserving a universal employee/contractor equivalence; specify the operative standard actually adopted rather than leaving lower courts an unexplained protection.
3. Accept a materially stronger speech-protection rule proposed by the contractor only if its departure from ordinary government-service balancing and its scope are justified. Do not silently treat the appellate rule as already that stronger rule.
4. Sustain the categorical contractor distinction, or a different lawful governmental-control ground within the presented scope, after confronting Perry, the valuable benefits lost, and the actual arrangement. A policy concern about initial bidding does not transform this case into an unsuccessful-new-bidder case.
5. Resolve a genuinely supported threshold issue if necessary; existing appellate standing and the assumed injury must be confronted rather than replaced by “five cities remained, therefore no injury.”

Any remand preserves personal immunity and McClure's separate judgment, ordinary capacity/attribution and damages requirements, and unresolved actual factual issues. It orders no automatic renewal, reinstatement, damages amount, complete immunity or trial. Neutral performance and service-based grounds remain available if actually proved. Initial competitive applicants, every future contracting decision and pure affiliation patronage are distinct scope questions; reservations decide none of them.

## Entering law, source boundary and participation

Research cutoff June28, 1996. The [preserved pre-June28 projection](../entering-law/OT_1995CHUNK10_PRE_19960628_NEUTRAL_PROJECTION.md) supplements the OT1994 baseline in [Speech Law](../entering-law/OT_1995CHUNK10_SPEECH_LAW.md). It supersedes the original section-I March18 cutoff. Incorporate completed earlier-effective chunk10 law through a neutral addendum before modeling; no result is assumed. June28 peers, including the other contractor case, do not govern each other. The cases are not treated as a secretly coordinated sequence.

All nine Justices were seated at argument and decision: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela; Stevens, O'Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg, Breyer. No case-specific nonparticipation is established. Six qualified Justices constitute a quorum and five of nine control a merits judgment.

The fresh validator read only governing neutral-stage instructions, authorized section-I sources, sanitized prior law/projection and the neutral source extraction. No raw Record, private position, current commitment, comparator, reconciliation, assignment or control/exposure file was consulted. Corrected factual/postural framing below replaces contrary generic shorthand in the original derived input, without editing the approved brief.

### Governing rules and available Justice-specific evidence

Pickering balances public-concern citizen speech against the government's legitimate service interests in the employment setting. Connick evaluates content, form and context and permits supported prospective operational concerns. Givhan recognizes that protected speech can be private. Perry separates the absence of entitlement to a benefit from withholding it for an unconstitutional reason. Mt. Healthy gives the claimant the substantial-or-motivating-factor showing and permits the government to prove by a preponderance that it would have made the same decision absent protected conduct. A possible lawful reason is not itself proof of that counterfactual.

Elrod, Branti and Rutan regulate patronage in their employee settings. Branti asks functionally whether political affiliation is an appropriate requirement for effective performance; a job title alone does not answer the question. These rules supply possible analogies and limits, not an already decided contractor holding.

**Rutan own-writing source map, verified pre-divergence authority:** Brennan's Court opinion was joined by Stevens; Stevens wrote separately. Scalia's dissent was joined by Kennedy throughout; O'Connor joined Parts II–III, excluding Part I's tradition-dispositive method. PartII challenges strict scrutiny in the employment relationship, discusses party benefits and coercion, and expressly argues against retaining Elrod/Branti; PartIII alternatively limits those cases to actual job loss and opposes expansion. Do not assign O'Connor PartI or erase her PartII-C position. No Rutan participation is attributed to Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg or Breyer. Sources: [official report, 497 U.S.62](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USREPORTS-497/pdf/USREPORTS-497-62.pdf), and [complete Scalia dissent](https://www.law.cornell.edu/supct/html/88-1872.ZD.html), including footnotes read by the source researcher. This map identifies competing prior grounds; it predicts no vote in this different setting.

**“Public-employee speech and the employer’s mistaken factual account,” Present operation effective Waters, May31, 1994:** O'Connor's plurality with Souter and Ginsburg (and the Chief Justice) supports the objective-reasonableness account. Scalia, Kennedy and Thomas's broader genuine-ground concurrence expressly accepts the narrower genuine-and-reasonable safe harbor. Stevens's actual-speech dissent supports the separately shared unreasonable-false-account limit. The limited majority propositions are controlling, but the full investigation framework has no majority and no universal independent investigation duty follows. Breyer was not on that Court. The exact current rule and coalition boundaries are copied below.

**“Prospective restrictions on employees’ citizen expression,” Present operation effective February22, 1995:** NTEU's broad prospective-burden rule is Stevens's PartI joined by Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer with the Chief Justice. O'Connor's separately identified case-specific Pickering agreement is not a join in the whole formulation. This honors the current Standards description; no unexamined separate rationale is attributed to Scalia or Thomas. NTEU concerns an advance honoraria ban and listeners as well as speakers; importing its precise justification allocation into an individual termination requires an explanation. The exact rule and limits are copied below.

**Settle, June25, 1996:** Souter's unanimous decision preserves genuine legitimate pedagogical authority while requiring actual causal examination under Mt. Healthy. Possible lawful reasons do not establish the same-decision defense. Its curricular rule and religious-viewpoint application do not become contractor rules; its express use of Waters's genuine-reliance distinction does preserve relevant causation continuity.

Kentucky v. Graham distinguishes entity/official-capacity claims from individual immunity. Monell retains its own attribution/liability requirements. A substantive speech ruling does not automatically establish those requirements, damages, an entitlement to continued business or a successful claim against every named defendant.

The model must use each Justice's own date-eligible writing or adopted public position at the actual level of agreement. Similarity of judgments is not a full rationale join. If a proposed material fork requires a prior writing not established here, obtain it before commitment; do not substitute a historical post-divergence version of NTEU or Waters.

## Source completeness and readiness

The attached neutral source excerpts were independently validated against the original submitted scope and current-law limits. Their complete lower-opinion reading and targeted original-document reading remain distinct. No claim of record absence, litigant default, waiver or conceded motive rests on unexamined pages. No new factual or procedural reconstruction premise is adopted.

Ready for independent non-Stone modeling of the supported constitutional scope and remedial alternatives, after the control-provided earlier-effective-law addendum is available if needed. No vote, result, assigned author or coalition is selected.
